research_question: Can a supervised model predict conditional grasp success from object geometry/properties, initial state and candidate grasp-control settings, under a declared distribution of execution uncertainty?
decision: Positive feasibility evidence for a multi-feature grasp-outcome modelling problem, not proof of model generalization or superiority to simple physical rules.
geometry_families: existing black-bowl collision geometry with rim grasp
existing wine-bottle collision geometry with neck grasp
controlled_setup_changes_from_original_d: Both target assets use the same nominal workspace position; storage furniture moved outside the workspace and the other object relocated.
Real collision and visual geometry uniformly scaled before compilation. Mass controlled separately, with inertia scaled consistently.
Sliding friction set on both target and finger contact geometries; torsional/rolling friction fixed to 0.005/0.0001, unlike the original asset settings.
Controller state machine unchanged; an experiment-local subclass exposes the closing tendon-force command. No original project source edited.
strong_evidence: Paired XYZ grasp-error draws uniform in [-6,+6] mm, ten draws per configuration and object: bowl 60 g / force command 4 N = 10/10; bowl 450 g / 4 N = 0/10; bowl 450 g / 8 N = 10/10.
With the SAME error draws: bottle 60 g / 4 N = 9/10; bottle 450 g / 4 N = 1/10; bottle 450 g / 8 N = 8/10.

Mass-friction-force factorial: at bowl mass 450 g, force command 8 N fails for mu 0.4 but succeeds for mu 0.8 at the nominal grasp pose; force command 4 N fails at both. This is a directly observed interaction, not a learned prediction.
preliminary_interaction_examples: At bottle mass 180 g and scale 0.7, opening 80 mm fails while 40 mm succeeds; at scale 1.0 and 1.3 both openings succeed. One trial per exact cell.

At bottle mass 180 g and speed setting 0.20 m/s, closure at arrival fails while triggering closure 10 mm above the grasp point succeeds. One trial per exact cell; sensitive to the strict bilateral-contact criterion.
probability_interpretation: Reported fractions are empirical frequencies over the declared execution-error distribution, with only ten draws each. They are not learned/calibrated probabilities, exact 0/1 probabilities, or universal physical success rates. The paired draws should remain grouped in any later train/test split.
label_quality_limit: All labels follow the existing strict controller and independent two-second hold observer. A momentary loss of bilateral contact can terminate a trial even when the object is elevated again at the next physics step. Some negative bottle labels are contact-criterion failures, not verified object drops. Label sensitivity should be audited before training at scale.
feature_observability_limit: Mass and friction are simulator ground truth; real deployment requires estimates or known values. The injected grasp-point bias is latent execution uncertainty, not automatically available as an observed input. Geometry class remains coupled to shape-specific rim/neck grasp profiles.
not_established: ML-based parameter selection improving actual execution
Benefit over simple friction/holding-force or geometry rules
Causal effect of semantic category alone
unexplored_candidates: clutter clearance as an explicit feature
next_step: Freeze an audited success label and observable feature list, collect grouped train/test conditions, compare a simple physical/rule baseline with a lightweight supervised model, and evaluate both probability quality and actual execution outcomes.
reproduction: Copy the three Python scripts to a NEW empty directory under this repository's results/ folder, then use .venv/bin/python to run run_exploration.py --phase smoke, run_exploration.py --phase screening, run_exploration.py --phase interactions, run_followups.py and analyze_exploration.py in that order. Existing phase directories are intentionally never overwritten. Protocols contain source hashes and the input/environment manifests.
